A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NPNet research and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and proofs.

before.justification: v3 reports original diffusion-model evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical experiments, including revised GenEval comparison results in Table 13.

M1.justification: Re-denoise sampling, preference-based data selection, singular-value and residual prediction, training losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3.

E1.justification: Both versions use Pick-a-Pic, DrawBench, HPD v2, and GenEval, plus the ImageNet fish-class evaluation and ControlNet scenarios. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Standard/Inversion, Repaint in Table 2, InitNO in Table 7, and DPO/AYS comparisons in Table 5. Table 13 revises existing comparators' scores without changing the comparator set.

E3.justification: The reported prompt subsets, model configurations, inference settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. No protocol revision is documented for the changed GenEval scores. Figure 1's metric rescaling changes their display only.

E4.justification: The architecture and data-selection ablations, hyperparameter studies, sampler and seed generalization analyses, and ControlNet case studies are retained with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Both report point estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty summaries.

E6.justification: Table 13 replaces all 24 Standard/Inversion scores across three diffusion models while retaining every NPNet score. SDXL Standard HPSv2 changes from 24.04 to 28.00, shrinking its reported gap to NPNet's 28.41 from 4.37 to 0.41. Hunyuan-DiT Standard HPSv2 changes from 27.78 to 30.46, reversing its comparison with SDXL+NPNet. Hunyuan-DiT NPNet PickScore now ties Standard at 23.15 and trails Inversion at 23.16. These substantially revise the GenEval margins and rankings; other experimental results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, DDIM/CFG equations, and Theorem E.1 with its proof are unchanged. Equation 6 moves between pages without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the claim that NPNet improves SDXL's GenEval HPSv2 by 18% and makes it surpass Hunyuan-DiT. The three principal contributions and broader quality, generalization, and efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and Appendix F's limitations concerning data quality, selection bias, and architecture design are unchanged. Appendix D.6 also retains its 'all improved metrics' interpretation despite the revised Table 13.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4's hyperparameters and hardware, the pseudocode, Figure 15's inference example, the repository link, and data-release statements are unchanged. No explanation of the GenEval score revisions is added.

R1.justification: The same 45 references and prior-noise-optimization discussions in Appendices B–C are retained, with unchanged novelty positioning as a learning framework. Bibliographic differences update citation-page backreferences.

P1.justification: Editing is limited principally to deleting the introductory GenEval example and updating the version/date header. Section order, methodological explanations, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is resized and rearranged, with HPSv2/ImageReward annotations rescaled by 100 and PickScore rounded; its example images are unchanged. Table 5 moves from page 8 to page 7, accompanied by text reflow. Table 13 retains its structure.

improvement.justification: Removing the 18% and cross-model superiority example aligns the introduction with v4's revised GenEval results. However, the baseline replacements are unexplained, so improved numerical accuracy cannot be established from the PDFs. Appendix D.6 also retains 'all improved metrics' despite Hunyuan-DiT PickScore now tying Standard and trailing Inversion. The narrower claim and presentation refinements therefore do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
